Assign a visible tube radius to line-only streamlines

Source: R/fatten.R
fatten.Rd

fatten() gives a fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, or fiber::bundle_set that carries no radius data a tube radius guaranteed to be visible to the naked eye, and stores it back on the object as a per-streamline radius key. Where plot3d() reports radius data the object already carries, and prune() thins a bundle down to a non-overlapping subset at a radius you choose, over which prune() gives you full control as the tunable engine. fatten() is the convenience wrapper that picks a radius for you and then reuses prune()'s selection logic internally for the dense case: afterwards a plain plot3d() call draws real 3D tubes. When you would rather pick the radius and the clearance between tubes yourself, call prune() directly instead.

The radius is chosen from the geometry of the streamlines themselves:

  • Sparse streamlines (far apart relative to the visibility floor) keep all their fibres and get a constant radius equal to half the minimal distance between any two streamlines, so adjacent tubes just touch and nothing is hidden.

  • Dense streamlines (packed closer than the floor) are pruned to a non-overlapping, hull-covering subset at the floor radius, preserving as many streamlines as can be shown without overlap at a visible size.

The visibility floor is the median distance between consecutive sampled points of the streamlines (the sampling density); a tube is treated as visible once its radius reaches that spacing. Override it with visibility.

Usage

fatten(x, visibility = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, or fiber::bundle_set.

visibility

Numeric. The smallest tube radius considered visible to the naked eye. NULL (default) derives it from the streamlines' sampling density (the median intra-streamline step); a positive number overrides the floor.

...

Reserved for future arguments.

Value

An object of the same class as x in which every streamline carries a per-streamline radius in its @streamline_data, so a subsequent plot3d() call renders real 3D tubes. For a dense fiber::bundle or fiber::bundle_set, the returned object holds the pruned (non-overlapping) subset of streamlines.

See also

prune(), plot3d()
